Name: Anselm of Canterbury
Summary: Benedictine monk and Archbishop of Canterbury, one of the great theologians of the medieval church.
Contribution: His Proslogion set out the famous argument for God's existence, and Cur Deus Homo gave the satisfaction account of atonement that shaped Western theology; he also defended the church's freedom against kings.
Testimony: He lived by faith seeking understanding, holding that belief comes first and reason serves to deepen what faith already holds.
